content.text:
I'm trying to open up my Jenkins CI installation on perlmutter_cpu, following the directions in ci/jenkins/README.perlmutter_gpu. However, when I get to this step

curl --fail --output /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8084/login

I get

  % Total    % Received % Xferd  Average Speed   Time    Time     Time  Current
                                 Dload  Upload   Total   Spent    Left  Speed
  0     0    0     0    0     0      0      0 --:--:-- --:--:-- --:--:--     0
curl: (7) Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1 port 8084 after 0 ms: Couldn't connect to server

why?
I’ll compare that readiness check with the Perlmutter setup instructions and identify what must be running or forwarded on the login node.

input.input:
const r = await tools.exec_command({"cmd":"sed -n '1,240p' .agents/skills/directory-structure/SKILL.md && sed -n '1,260p' ci/jenkins/README.perlmutter_gpu","workdir":"/Users/mfrancis/Documents/gkeyll/code/gkeyll_v1/gkeyll","yield_time_ms":10000,"max_output_tokens":20000});
text(r.output);

text(r.output);

content.text:
`127.0.0.1:8084` exists only on your laptop after the SSH tunnel is running. A connection refusal means that tunnel is not listening there—most commonly because the `curl` was run on Perlmutter rather than locally, or the `ssh -L` command failed/exited.

On the Perlmutter login node that hosts Jenkins, check the controller itself on port 8080:

```sh
curl --fail --output /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8080/login
tmux attach -t gkeyll_ci
```

If that succeeds, record the exact node:

```sh
hostname -f
```

Then run this from your laptop terminal (not from Perlmutter), substituting that hostname:

```sh
ssh -f -N -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes \
  -J <username>@perlmutter.nersc.gov \
  -L 127.0.0.1:8084:127.0.0.1:8080 \
  <username>@loginXX.chn.perlmutter.nersc.gov
```

Now, still on the laptop:

```sh
curl --fail --output /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8084/login
```

If the remote `:8080` check fails, Jenkins did not start or died; inspect `tmux attach -t gkeyll_ci` and `$GKEYLL_CI_ROOT/logs/jenkins.log`.

The checks on the perlmutter

curl --fail --output /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8080/login
  tmux attach -t gkeyll_ci

succeeded, meaning I didn't see anything wrong there. Then I did

ssh -f -N -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes \
                 -J mana@perlmutter.nersc.gov \
             mana@login23.chn.perlmutter.nersc.gov

but

curl --fail --output /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8084/login

on my laptop still failed.

The jenkins.log is here: ~/Downloads/jenkins.log

Your SSH command is missing the port-forwarding option. It only logs into `login23` in the background; it never creates a listener on laptop port 8084.

Run this from your laptop:

```sh
ssh -f -N -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes \
  -J mana@perlmutter.nersc.gov \
  -L 127.0.0.1:8084:127.0.0.1:8080 \
  mana@login23.chn.perlmutter.nersc.gov
```

Then:

```sh
curl --fail --output /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8084/login
```

Since the remote `127.0.0.1:8080/login` test succeeds, the Jenkins log is not needed for this particular issue.
